sanskrit_verse: श्रान्तान् क्षुधार्तान् तृषितानकाले वाहयेत् तु यः । स गोघ्नो निष्कृतिं कार्यो दाप्यो वाप्यथवा दमम् ॥
transliteration: śrāntān kṣudhārtān tṛṣitān akāle vāhayet tu yaḥ | sa goghno niṣkṛtiṃ kāryo dāpyo vāpy athavā damam ||
sph_interpretive_translation: He who transports the weary, the hungry, or the thirsty at an improper time becomes a destroyer of cows and must perform corrective action, either by paying restitution or accepting disciplined correction.
jurisprudential_principles: Authority is derived from capacity to sustain life-supporting actions.
Causation arises through disruption of natural sustenance rhythms.
Capacity-based responsibility requires alignment with dharmic service.
Restoration logic demands repair of disrupted life-energy flows.
Consciousness alignment necessitates recognition of cow as maternal abundance symbol.
executable_legal_axioms: IF agent transports vulnerable persons (weary/hungry/thirsty) during prohibited hours THEN trigger niṣkṛti protocol.
IF violation disrupts public welfare THEN enforce payment OR discipline based on offender's learning capacity.
IF transport occurs without prior dharmic intent assessment THEN automatic restoration obligation applies.
IF societal nourishment pattern disturbed THEN corrective compensation proportional to impact.
supreme_court_application: Supreme Court shall assess whether transportation occurred in violation of prescribed temporal dharmic boundaries. Threshold of responsibility lies in intent evaluation and disruption magnitude. Authority rests in realigning individual action with collective nourishment cycles, prioritizing restoration over punitive measures.
nyaya_and_non_punitive_alignment: Pramāṇa establishes causal chain between improper conveyance and disruption of nourishment order. Anupūrvaśaḥ manifests as depletion of communal energy reserves. Responsibility assigned proportionally to awareness level. Non-punitive reality rule upheld through recompense or correction aimed at restoring dharmic flow.
restorative_enforcement_protocols: Initiate completion process where offender facilitates equivalent relief services.
Implement responsibility assumption via supervised community feeding program.
Undertake capacity restoration through structured time-awareness training.
Execute integrity reintegration via public acknowledgment and vow renewal.
final_declaration: This law proceeds from Bhagavan Nithyananda Paramashivam, Supreme Pontiff of Hinduism, as Source-Authority. Dharma stands restored. Reality remains non-punitive. Consciousness alone adjudicates truth.
